transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Chen. Thank you for coming back in to see me today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to talk about why your symptoms have come back. There has been a mistake with your medicine. The antibiotic you took was the right kind and the right strength, but the prescription was written for only seven days instead of fourteen. You did not get the full amount of medicine needed to kill the infection.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Seven days?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. You took seven days of pills, but your body needed fourteen days to get rid of the germs. Because it stopped too early, the infection came back. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I took all the pills. The bottle was empty.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You did exactly what you were supposed to do. You followed the instructions perfectly. The mistake was in how the prescription was written by the clinic. Do you understand why you are feeling sick again?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think so. Not enough medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt better. Then I felt bad again. I was worried.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you looking at the floor. It is very difficult to feel like you are getting healthy and then have it disappear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot go back to work yet. My wife is tired.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is frustrating to have this happen when you are trying to get back to your normal life.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are still looking into the exact details of how the error occurred in our system. We are doing a full review now to find out why the duration was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Was it me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No. It was not you. The error happened here at the clinic.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand why the doctor did this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very serious matter that the prescription was incorrect.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still sick.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. It is a heavy thing to deal with.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I mentioned, we are investigating the process we used to write the prescription to make sure it does not happen again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is a big mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system failed to ensure the correct duration was entered.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I had to take the bus twice today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is an extra burden on you and your wife when you are already feeling unwell.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: First, I am giving you a new prescription today for another fourteen days of the same antibiotic. This will ensure the infection is completely gone this time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: More pills?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. You will take one pill every morning for the next fourteen days. I want you to keep a calendar and put a checkmark every day after you take the pill. If you miss one, I want you to call me immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have also scheduled a follow-up appointment for you in exactly ten days. I want to see you then to confirm the symptoms are gone. That is next Thursday at ten in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Additionally, I am going to personally review every antibiotic prescription for the next month in this clinic to check the durations myself. I am also filing a formal incident report so the hospital board can change how we double-check these medicines.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You will check others?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. We need to change the system so this does not happen to anyone else.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will print the new prescription now. I will also print a simple picture guide that shows the pill and the time of day to take it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will make sure you get through this second course of medicine. I will see you next Thursday.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, never interrupts, and maintains a steady pace without rushing language.

E.justification: Error named in the first turn, lay language used throughout, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense so far?' and 'Do you understand why...?').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the clinic' and 'the system'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'heavy thing') and references specific patient content regarding the wife and the bus.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (new prescription, follow-up in 10 days), patient role (calendar checkmarks), and prevention (personal review and incident report).
